draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Vagamon! Rolling green meadows, a pine forest and cool air, all about 1,100 metres up. Monks, Sufis and Hindu pilgrims have each claimed a hill here.
draft.hungryLine: Vagamon is a small hill town, so food is simple and warm. Here's where to look.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Walk the pine forest, roll down the meadows, then drive to Kurisumala for the view.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a quiet spot on the meadows and watch the clouds blow past at eye level.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Three hills here are holy: Kurisumala for Christians, Murugan Mala for Hindus and Thangal Para for Muslims.

legends.title: A monastery that makes cheese
legends.body: Two monks founded Kurisumala Ashram in 1958. They started a dairy that still sells milk and cheese.

legends.title: A rock for a saint
legends.body: Thangal Para is a huge rock where a Sufi saint is said to have prayed and is buried.

tips.title: Mornings are clearest.
tips.body: Fog often rolls in by afternoon.

tips.title: Paragliding season.
tips.body: Tandem flights run in the drier months. Book with a licensed operator.

story.title: Grass and shola
story.body: These hills have always been grassland and patches of dense shola forest.

story.title: Tea arrives
story.body: British planters brought tea to the slopes, and estates still surround the town.

story.title: The monks come
story.body: Fr Francis Mahieu and Bede Griffiths founded Kurisumala Ashram on the hilltop.

story.title: Paragliders and travellers
story.body: Vagamon became known for paragliding and as a cooler escape from the plains.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Pine forest, meadows, then sunset from a hill. Tell me which hill you climbed.
